subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Yolk Sac Tumour and Granulosa Cell Neoplasia

steps.tx: The second most common malignant ovarian germ cell neoplasm is **yolk sac tumour**, historically referred to as endodermal sinus tumor. Characterized by explosive clinical growth and extensive pelvic pain, it occurs predominantly in children and young women around eighteen years of age. Rapid peritoneal and lymphatic spread requires prompt aggressive multimodality management.
steps.say: Yolk sac tumor is a rapidly growing germ cell malignancy presenting with acute pelvic pain in young females.

steps.tx: The absolute diagnostic and surveillance marker secreted by yolk sac tumors is **elevated alpha fetoprotein**. Serum AFP concentrations frequently reach thousands of nanograms per milliliter, paralleling total viable tumor burden. A post-resection decline matching the five-day metabolic half-life of AFP indicates complete surgical resection, while persistent elevation indicates residual microscopic disease.
steps.say: Alpha-fetoprotein is the pathognomonic serum marker for yolk sac tumor and guides therapeutic response.

steps.tx: Microscopic examination reveals the diagnostic pathognomonic hallmark termed **Schiller Duval bodies**. These perivascular structures consist of a central core containing a solitary thin-walled capillary vessel enveloped by primitive cuboidal tumor cells, projecting into an amphitheater-like space lined by flattened endothelial-like cells. Intracytoplasmic PAS-positive diastase-resistant hyaline globules containing AFP are also abundant.
steps.say: Schiller-Duval bodies consist of central capillaries surrounded by malignant cells inside cystic spaces.

steps.tx: Immediate postoperative management requires combination chemotherapy with **bleomycin etoposide cisplatin**. Prior to the development of platinum regimens, yolk sac tumor was uniformly fatal. Modern three to four cycle BEP therapy achieves cure rates exceeding eighty-five percent. Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with comprehensive staging preserves fertility in most young women.
steps.say: Combination BEP chemotherapy transformed yolk sac tumor from a lethal disease into a curable condition.

steps.tx: The most common malignant sex cord-stromal neoplasm of the ovary is **granulosa cell tumour**, representing two to five percent of all ovarian cancers. Classified into juvenile and adult forms, the adult subtype typically arises in perimenopausal and postmenopausal women around fifty-five years of age. Unlike epithelial cancers, it follows an indolent course with late recurrences.
steps.say: Granulosa cell tumor is an indolent estrogenic sex cord neoplasm with a tendency for late recurrences.

vis.alt: Histopathology of granulosa cell tumor displaying Call-Exner bodies.
vis.caption: Granulosa cell tumor histology showing Call-Exner bodies and grooved nuclei. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Autonomous secretion of estradiol by functioning neoplastic granulosa cells triggers **hyperestrogenic clinical manifestations**. In prepubertal girls, juvenile granulosa cell tumor provokes isosexual precocious pseudopuberty. In postmenopausal women, prolonged estrogen excess stimulates the endometrium, presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding, endometrial hyperplasia, or concurrent well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
steps.say: Estrogen secretion by granulosa cell tumors causes precocious puberty in girls and postmenopausal bleeding in women.

rows: Endometrial cancer in up to 10 percent

steps.tx: Histopathological diagnosis depends on identifying pale round nuclei with central longitudinal grooves, termed **coffee bean nuclei**. Cells cluster into microfollicular structures containing central eosinophilic fluid and pyknotic nuclear debris, named Call-Exner bodies. Somatic missense mutations in the transcription factor FOXL2 (C402G) occur in over ninety-five percent of adult granulosa cell tumors.
steps.say: Coffee bean grooved nuclei, Call-Exner bodies, and FOXL2 mutations characterize granulosa cell tumors.

vis.alt: Micrograph of granulosa cell tumor showing nuclear features and Call-Exner bodies.
vis.caption: Granulosa cell tumor histology displaying coffee bean nuclei and Call-Exner microfollicles. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Surgical management in postmenopausal patients requires **total abdominal hysterectomy** and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Endometrial sampling is mandatory prior to surgery to exclude coexisting endometrial hyperplasia or adenocarcinoma. Because recurrences commonly arise ten to twenty years following initial resection, patients require lifelong clinical and biochemical surveillance.
steps.say: Lifelong surveillance is mandatory for granulosa cell tumors due to their propensity for late recurrence.
